blind_spots_patched: Original Chapters 3 and 6 treated MCX's post-TCS cost structure as overwhelmingly fixed and cited a 21.2% FY26 effective tax rate without accounting for three ongoing earnings-conversion frictions: (1) volume-linked CME Group benchmark license fees (~10% of energy contract revenue, ₹107.96 Cr in FY26) that rise proportionally with crude oil turnover; (2) recurring IT opex stepping up to fund 2x processing capacity and cybersecurity; and (3) a structural step-up in normalized effective tax rate toward ~25% alongside the temporary nature of Q2 FY27's zero SGF contribution holiday.

Original Chapter 6 cited a 27%–65% historical dividend payout while overlooking that FY26 payout compressed sharply to 15% of PAT as reserves swelled to ₹3,461 crore, and original Chapters 1 and 5 omitted SEBI's May 2025 ₹25 lakh enforcement penalty on MCX for material disclosure lapses regarding 63 Moons software payments.
assumptions_changed: WEAKENED: Post-TCS IT expenses settled into a static fixed-cost annual band of ₹90–110 crore (₹104.74 crore in FY26), letting incremental volume flow through with minimal recurring tech cost growth.
CONFIRMED: Core options and futures volumes, active F&O client breadth (14.98 lakh in Q2 FY27), Silver 100g (>₹100 Cr ADT), and Electricity Futures (~75% share at ₹77 Cr ADT) are scaling rapidly.
CONFIRMED: MCXCCL's Core Settlement Guarantee Fund (₹1,367.29 crore in FY26) and SEBI's Z-score adjustments ease near-term SGF top-up needs while preserving a zero-debt fortress balance sheet.
CONFIRMED: MCX's turnover remains heavily concentrated in bullion and energy (>97% of F&O ADT), creating sensitivity to commodity volatility regimes and FPI access constraints.
